deep.reconstruction:
PURPOSE. This is an 1818 latitude (polar height) determination at the Göttingen observatory with the Repsold meridian circle. The star is α Arietis, observed at upper culmination in two circle positions; the previous page is headed 'Repsold's Kreis'. The header gives α ≈ 29°14'6" (right ascension in degrees, about 1h57m) and δ ≈ 22°35'55" (approximate declination). The header numbers −0.48379, +0.0812 and 2707.33 are auxiliary; their meaning is uncertain. The pink '45.' is the folio number.

TABLE COLUMNS.
- Date and circle reading (apparent zenith distance z').
- Barometer, in Paris inches and lines (27 in 10.0 lines, etc.).
- Attached thermometer and outside thermometer, in °Réaumur.
- Two columns whose sum is Bessel's day number A (a time argument plus a nutation part).
- Two columns whose sum is B (nutation).
- C (aberration).
- D (aberration).

Group I (Jun 26, 27; one circle position).
- Mean z' = (50.31+48.19)/2 → 28°55'49.25".
- Barometer 27 in 8.45 lines; attached thermometer 15.2 (exactly 15.25); outside 13.15.
- A = mean(0.4889−0.1943, 0.4923−0.1940) = 0.29645.
- B = mean(−7.26+0.43, −7.26+0.42) = −6.835.
- C = +1.795; D = −20.515.

Group II (Jun 29, Jul 8, 9, 18; circle reversed).
- Readings are written with seconds ≥ 60, e.g. 28°54'60.70" = 28°55'0.70".
- Mean z' = 28°54'59.30" (exactly 59.2975).
- Barometer 27 in 8.82 lines; thermometers 14.7 and 10.75.
- A = 0.33927 (exactly 0.339275); B = −6.965; C = +5.445; D = −19.617 (exactly −19.6175).

REFRACTION (Bessel 1818 form, r = α tan z · barometer and temperature factors).
- log α = 1.75998 (α ≈ 57.54", i.e. Bessel's Fundamenta Astronomiae value at this zenith distance; the next page has 1.75970 at z ≈ 43°).
- log tan(28°55'24") = 9.74238. The argument is the mean of the two groups, 28°55'24.27".
- Sum: 1.50236.
- Barometric log corrections: −180 (group I) and −127 (group II), in units of the 5th decimal. They plausibly come from reducing the barometer, corrected for mercury temperature, to the normal 29.6 English inches; this is my inference.
- Thermometer log corrections: −1146 and −667, about 200 units per °R above the normal ≈ 7.4°R (48.75°F); also my inference.
- Results: log r = 1.48910 → r = 30.84"; log r = 1.49442 → r = 31.22".

REDUCTION APPARENT → MEAN DECLINATION (Bessel day numbers and star constants).
- Δδ = A·a' + B·b' + C·c' + D·d', with:
  - a' = n cos α, where log n = 1.30198 (n = 20.045", annual precession in declination);
  - b' = −sin α;
  - c' = tan ε cos δ − sin α sin δ;
  - d' = cos α sin δ.
- Auxiliary logs:
  - 1: log n = 1.30198
  - 2: log cos α = 9.94083
  - 3: log sin δ = 9.58464
  - 4: log sin α = 9.68875
  - 5: log cos δ = 9.96530
  - 6: log tan ε = 9.63756 (ε ≈ 23°27'50")
- Then:
  - log(tanε cosδ) = 9.60286;
  - log(sinα sinδ) = 9.27339 (with n, i.e. negative);
  - their difference gives log c' = 9.32852;
  - log a' = 1.30198 + 9.94083 = 1.24281;
  - log b' = 9.68875n;
  - log d' = 9.94083 + 9.58464 = 9.52547.
- The struck 8.97020 under it is the d' value from the ε Tauri page, copied by mistake.
- The row logs are log(A−1), log B, log C, log D for each group:
  - Group I: 9.84729n (A−1 = −0.70355), 0.83474n, 0.25406, 1.31207n.
  - Group II: 9.82002n (A−1 = −0.66073), 0.84292n, 0.73600, 1.29263n.
  - The −1 is presumably a shift of epoch by one year (my inference).
- Products, group I: −12.305, +3.338, +0.382, −6.879; sum −15.46.
- Products, group II: −11.557, +3.401, +1.160, −6.578; sum −13.57.
- The struck −1.915 and −1.832 are the d' terms computed with the wrong 8.97020.
- Right-hand partial sums:
  - −8.967 = −12.305+3.338; −8.156 = −11.557+3.401;
  - −6.497 = 0.382−6.879; −5.418 = 1.160−6.578;
  - the struck −1.533 and −0.672 are the same sums with the wrong d'.

FINAL REDUCTION.
- Group I: 28°55'49.25" + 30.84" = 28°56'20.09"; then −15.46" = 28°56'4.63".
- Group II: 28°54'59.30" + 31.22" = 28°55'30.52"; then −13.57" (replacing a struck 14.94) = 28°55'16.95".
- A first index error of 23.95" was struck. Final: index error = (4.63+60−16.95)/2 = 23.84".
- True zenith distance z = mean = 28°55'40.79".
- A preliminary unreduced mean 28°55'55.30" sits next to the assumed latitude 51°31'50".
- The star's mean polar distance is p = 67°23'52.11" (δ = 22°36'7.89").
- Latitude φ = 90° − p + z = 22°36'7.89" + 28°55'40.79" = 51°31'48.68".
- Compare: ε Tauri on the previous page gives 51°31'47.68"; α Aquilae on the next page gives 51°31'47.95".
errors: No substantive arithmetic error in the final figures. All means, refraction antilogs, log sums, the four products and their sums, the index error, and the final latitude check.

The d' coefficient was first copied from the ε Tauri page (8.97020) and corrected by Gauss to 9.52547. This changed the fourth reduction terms from −1.915 and −1.832 to −6.879 and −6.578, and hence the correction for group II from a struck 14.94 to 13.57.
A first index-error value of 23.95" (from an intermediate, partly overwritten value) was superseded by 23.84".
Rounding: 15.25 is entered as 15.2, and 59.2975 as 59.30. These are harmless.

Unresolved, not necessarily an error: the A-column part (0.4889 … 0.5612) advances about 0.0033 per day, faster than a simple fraction of the year (0.00274 per day). The header numbers +0.0812 and −0.48379 may be scale factors involved. Their meaning is unclear to me.

results.what: Refraction r = α tan z with barometric and thermometric log corrections (log α = 1.75998), giving 30.84" and 31.22".
Reduction of apparent to mean declination as Aa'+Bb'+Cc'+Dd' with a' = n cos α, b' = −sin α, c' = tanε cosδ − sinα sinδ, d' = cosα sinδ.
results.modern_name: Besselian day numbers and star constants
results.usually_credited_to: F. W. Bessel (systematized in Tabulae Regiomontanae, 1830; precursors in Fundamenta Astronomiae, 1818)

results.what: Elimination of the circle's index error by observing in two circle positions; latitude φ = δ + z.
results.modern_name: Latitude from meridian zenith distances with circle reversal

results.what: Latitude of the Göttingen observatory, 51°31'48.68" from α Arietis.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observational reduction: refraction, day-number reduction to mean place, index error and latitude. The only mild point of interest is that the full four-term star-constant scheme (a', b', c', d' with A, B, C, D) appears in Gauss's reductions of 1818 observations, before Bessel's 1830 Tabulae Regiomontanae. However, the date of the computation is not certain, and similar forms circulated earlier.

checkable.asserts: log c' = log(tanε cosδ − sinα sinδ) ≈ 9.32852
the row logs 9.84729 and 9.82002 are log(1−A)

transcription_corrections: '+2.401' should be +3.401 (log 9.68875n + 0.84292n); the sums −8.156 and −13.57 require it.
The struck '[-1.533 0,672-]' is −1.533 and −0.672 (c' + d' terms computed with the wrong d').
The header '45.' (in pink) is the folio number, not data.

'28.55.49,25 + 30,84 ...' line: the final value 28.56.4,63 appears written over an earlier value (possibly 4.69). In the second line the struck 14.94 is replaced by 13.57, and the result 28.55.16,95 is written over a struck intermediate.
